semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Epidemic modeling is closely aligned with infectious disease epidemiology, as it involves understanding and predicting the patterns and spread of diseases within populations.

parent_domains.justification: Modeling is a broad domain that encompasses various types of modeling, including epidemic modeling.
Epidemic modeling often involves mathematical techniques to simulate the spread of diseases, fitting under the broader category of mathematical modeling.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Modeling is the most general and encompassing field that epidemic modeling falls under, as it involves creating representations of systems or processes.

child_domains.justification: Outbreak detection is a specific application within epidemic modeling that focuses on identifying occurrences of disease spread.
Disease surveillance involves monitoring the spread of diseases and can be considered a specific aspect of epidemic modeling.
Predictive modeling in public health can include epidemic modeling to forecast the progression of diseases in populations.

closest_child_domain.justification: Outbreak detection is directly related to epidemic modeling, as it involves identifying and monitoring outbreaks, which are critical components of managing epidemics.

sibling_domains.justification: Graphical models can represent probabilistic relationships and are related to modeling approaches used in epidemic context.
Probabilistic modeling is a technique used to handle uncertainty in epidemic modeling.
Temporal modeling involves time-based predictions, which are often necessary in tracking and forecasting epidemics.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Probabilistic modeling is closely related to epidemic modeling as it is often used to incorporate uncertainty and variability in disease spread predictions.

unrelated_domains.justification: Species distribution modeling focuses on the spatial distribution of species, which is unrelated to the spread of diseases in populations.
Ecological modeling involves the study of ecosystems, which is generally unrelated to epidemic modeling.
Graph-based modeling is a way to represent systems that may not necessarily align with the specific needs of epidemic modeling, despite some overlap in representing networks.
Diffusion models concern the general concept of diffusion, which may not directly pertain to disease spread without additional context.
These models are broader and not specifically tied to the intricacies of epidemic or disease modeling.
Latent diffusion models don't inherently relate to epidemic dynamics unless specified within the context of disease spread.
Sequence modeling often deals with ordered data sequences, unrelated to the public health focus of epidemic modeling.
